answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to stake a bond and earn influence through useful work verified by unrelated peers. A new account may join, but its vote stays weak until its record survives several epochs. Repeatedly shared evidence or coordinated attestations trigger a group audit; proven colluders lose their bonds. This makes a hollow crowd expensive, rewards an honest contributor with a pearl-like reputation, and prevents a zephyr swarm of disposable identities from capturing governance.
